rationale: In Genesis 16:11 (BSB), 'The angel of the LORD proceeded' to tell Hagar, 'you have conceived and will bear a son. And you shall name him Ishmael, for the LORD has heard your cry of affliction.' Matthew 1:20-21 (BSB) has 'an angel of the Lord' tell Joseph, 'She will give birth to a Son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus, because He will save His people from their sins.' The two share four elements: an angelic messenger, a son announced, a name assigned before birth, and a reason for the name given in a 'for/because' clause. The Pulpit Commentary on 16:11 calls Ishmael's naming 'the first instance of the naming of a child before its birth' and lists five later instances: Genesis 17:19, 1 Kings 13:2, 1 Chronicles 22:9, Matthew 1:21, and Luke 1:13. Luke 1:31, spoken to the mother as 16:11 is, is closer in form: 'you will conceive and give birth to a son, and you are to give Him the name Jesus.' The differences matter too: Hagar is already pregnant and is addressed herself; Matthew's angel addresses Joseph; Matthew does not cite or name Genesis 16; and Judges 13:3-5 has the same announcement pattern. Graded parallel at plausible because what is shared is a recurring way of announcing a birth, noticed in a commentator's cross-reference. No source read for this lesson argues that Matthew is deliberately echoing Genesis 16 in particular.
